note: Worked example transcript for the P4 writer lane gate: a recorded model session for Maren (adult pack), kink 'hypnosis', stage 3, replayed through the fixture transport. Estate-authored fixture text; the live transport is exercised separately against a local endpoint.

responses.d1: Nurse Maren, I have kept every appointment this week, every single one, and my hands still shake when the session bell rings. Please, tell me plainly what today's session is for, because I do better when I know the shape of the hour before it begins.
responses.d2: Then we begin the way we always begin. Sit down, set your shoulders against the chair, and let your breathing slow until it matches mine. You have learned this posture so well that your body finds it before your thoughts catch up, and that is exactly the progress we planned.
responses.d3: Good. Hold that stillness a moment longer, and hear me clearly: the calm you feel is yours, earned one session at a time, and it stays with you when you leave this room. Steady hands, steady heart. That is the whole of the lesson, and you already know it by heart.
responses.prose: The session room keeps its own quiet: one lamp, one chair, the soft tick of the wall clock marking a tempo slower than the corridor outside. Maren reviews the chart before she speaks, because the chart is a promise she made to herself years ago — that no session would ever run on habit alone, that every step of the conditioning would be written down, witnessed, and reversible at a word. Her patient sits where she indicated, hands folded, breathing already beginning to settle into the rhythm the room teaches. She counts the breaths without moving her lips. Four in, six out. The induction is not a trick and she would resent anyone calling it one; it is attention, trained the way a musician trains a scale, until the body trusts the pattern enough to rest inside it. When she speaks, her voice stays at the register she uses for frightened patients on night rounds, level and unhurried, and she watches the shoulders drop the way they always drop at this stage. Obedience training, in her private notes, is a misleading name for what she actually does here: she is teaching a nervous system that stillness is safe, that instruction can be a shelter rather than a threat. The chart will record the stage reached, the words used, the exact minute the trance took hold. Nothing about the hour will live only in memory. That, too, is part of the care.
